questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $A$ on a horizontal plane with speed $50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle of elevation $\alpha$ so that it passes through the point $(120, 10)$. Show that there are two possible angles of projection.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Take the origin at $A$, the $x$-axis horizontal in the plane of motion and the $y$-axis vertically upwards. The only force is the weight (no air resistance), so the horizontal velocity stays $50\cos\alpha$ and the vertical acceleration is $-g$, with $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Coordinates are in metres.

$$x = 50\cos\alpha\; t,\qquad y = 50\sin\alpha\; t - \tfrac12 g t^2$$

Eliminate $t = \dfrac{x}{50\cos\alpha}$ and use $\dfrac{1}{\cos^2\alpha} = 1 + \tan^2\alpha$:

$$y = x\tan\alpha - \frac{g x^2}{2\times 50^2\cos^2\alpha} = x\tan\alpha - \frac{g x^2}{5000}\,(1 + \tan^2\alpha)$$

The path passes through $(120, 10)$. Put $T = \tan\alpha$:

$$10 = 120\,T - \frac{9.8\times 14\,400}{5000}(1 + T^2) = 120\,T - 28.224\,(1 + T^2)$$

$$28.224\,T^2 - 120\,T + 38.224 = 0$$

**Discriminant:**

$$\Delta = 120^2 - 4(28.224)(38.224) = 14\,400 - 4315.3 = 10\,084.7 > 0$$

So the quadratic in $\tan\alpha$ has two distinct real roots. Both are positive (sum of roots $\tfrac{120}{28.224} > 0$, product $\tfrac{38.224}{28.224} > 0$), so each gives an angle of elevation between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$:

$$T = \frac{120 \pm \sqrt{10\,084.7}}{2\times 28.224} \;\Rightarrow\; \tan\alpha = 3.905 \text{ or } 0.347,\qquad \alpha \approx 75.6^\circ \text{ or } 19.1^\circ$$

**Hence there are two possible angles of projection**, about $19.1^\circ$ and $75.6^\circ$ (with $g = 10$: $19.5^\circ$ and $75.3^\circ$).

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $A$ on a horizontal plane with speed $50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle of projection of $30^\circ$. Find the maximum height.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Vertical motion only, upwards positive, $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Initial vertical velocity $u_y = 50\sin 30^\circ = 25\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. At the highest point $v_y = 0$:

$$v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2gH \;\Rightarrow\; 0 = 25^2 - 2(9.8)H \;\Rightarrow\; H = \frac{625}{19.6} = 31.9\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Maximum height $\approx 31.9\ \mathrm{m}$** above the point of projection ($31.25\ \mathrm{m}$ with $g = 10$).

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $A$ on a horizontal plane with speed $50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle of projection of $30^\circ$. Find the range of the particle on the horizontal plane through the point of projection.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The particle lands again when $y = 0$, at time $T_f$ (see part (d)). With the horizontal velocity $50\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$:

$$R = 50\cos30^\circ\times T_f = \frac{u^2\sin 2\alpha}{g} = \frac{2500\,\sin 60^\circ}{9.8} = \frac{2500\times 0.8660}{9.8} = 220.9\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Range $\approx 221\ \mathrm{m}$** ($216.5\ \mathrm{m}$ with $g = 10$).

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $A$ on a horizontal plane with speed $50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle of projection of $30^\circ$. Find the time of flight.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The particle is back on the horizontal plane when $y = 0$: $25\,t - 4.9\,t^2 = 0$, so $t = 0$ (launch) or

$$t = \frac{25}{4.9} = \frac{2u\sin\alpha}{g} = \frac{50}{9.8} = 5.10\ \mathrm{s}$$

**Time of flight $\approx 5.10\ \mathrm{s}$** ($5\ \mathrm{s}$ with $g = 10$).

(Check: range $= 25\sqrt3\times 5.102 = 220.9\ \mathrm{m}$, as in part (c).)

questions.enonce_markdown: The velocity of a particle $A$ relative to particle $B$ is $(2\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the velocity of particle $C$ relative to $A$ is $(5\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find the velocity of $C$ relative to $B$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Relative velocities add like vectors along a chain: $\mathbf{v}_{C/B} = \mathbf{v}_C - \mathbf{v}_B = (\mathbf{v}_C - \mathbf{v}_A) + (\mathbf{v}_A - \mathbf{v}_B) = \mathbf{v}_{C/A} + \mathbf{v}_{A/B}$.

$$\mathbf{v}_{C/B} = (5\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j}) + (2\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j}) = (7\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

**The velocity of $C$ relative to $B$ is $(7\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$** (magnitude $\sqrt{58} \approx 7.62\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$).
